purpose: Generator seed for armor-making materials, tools, techniques, and output armor family proxies.
coordinate_assumption: Attach armor outputs to human anatomy landmarks; tools are workshop props unless marked as applied technique.

workflow.output: curved plates, padded channels, laced grids
workflow.generator_target: deformed shells, quilt grids, ring/scale arrays
constraints and motion clearance debug volumes
material masks and surface detail layers

entries.name: linen canvas
entries.historical_notes: Common textile base for padded defenses and linings; also useful as a cover layer over plates.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate as thin cloth shell with visible weave normal map and seam-edge stitch curves.

entries.name: wool cloth
entries.used_for: padding, cloaks, lining, cold-weather arming wear
entries.historical_notes: Wool compresses into useful padding and accepts dye well; good for non-metal armor layers.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use soft matte material with fuzz shader, quilt channels, and thickness bevel.

entries.name: cotton batting
entries.historical_notes: Use as a general padding proxy, even where linen tow, wool, or other fibers would be more period-specific.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Represent as slightly inflated panels between stitched seam lines.

entries.name: leather hide
entries.used_for: straps, belts, lamellar backing, light armor panels
entries.historical_notes: Leather appears across many armor systems, especially as backing, suspension, edging, and straps.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate panels with beveled thickness, grain bump, edge darkening, and stitch holes.

entries.name: rawhide
entries.used_for: hardened strips, shield facing, scale/lamella proxies
entries.historical_notes: Rawhide can dry into stiff structural shapes; useful for historic non-metal defenses.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use tan translucent-ish rough material, warped panel edges, and cord-lacing holes.

entries.name: horn
entries.used_for: small plates, reinforced edges, decorative inserts
entries.historical_notes: Horn is historically plausible for small fittings and composite defensive pieces.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use thin curved plates with amber/brown shader and layered translucency.

entries.name: bone
entries.used_for: decorative mounts, small fasteners, ritual/fantasy armor details
entries.historical_notes: Better as decorative or small hardware in this generator, not primary armor structure.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use off-white carved plates with pores and softened edges.

entries.name: bronze sheet
entries.historical_notes: Bronze was prominent in many ancient armor traditions before iron/steel plate dominance.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use warm metal shader, hammered normal detail, green patina mask option.

entries.name: copper alloy fittings
entries.historical_notes: Copper alloys suit visible decorative fittings and contrast against iron or leather.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate rivet domes, edging strips, buckle frames, and ornamental plates.

entries.name: iron plate
entries.historical_notes: Iron plates vary greatly by period and quality; use as a broad historical proxy.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Dark rough metal material with pitting, uneven hammer texture, and edge wear.

entries.name: steel plate
entries.historical_notes: Better for articulated plate, helmets, gauntlets, and greaves in later armor families.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use reflective metal shader, procedural scratches, bevel highlights, and curvature maps.

entries.name: spring steel strip
entries.historical_notes: Useful generic material category for narrow reinforcing strips and fantasy mechanisms.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate repeat strip arrays with rivets and curvature following limbs.

entries.name: iron wire
entries.used_for: mail rings, edging links, suspension links
entries.historical_notes: Mail production begins with wire or drawn rod; ring pattern matters more visually than exact metallurgy.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use curve bevel_depth for wire; instance torus rings for mail patches.

entries.name: riveted mail ring
entries.historical_notes: Riveted rings are common in robust historical mail; avoid modeling every ring unless close-up.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use instanced flattened torus with tiny rivet cap; LOD swap to texture far away.

entries.name: solid mail ring
entries.historical_notes: Solid rings can appear mixed with riveted rings; useful as a simplified generator element.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Instance torus rings in 4-in-1 pattern or bake to normal map.

entries.name: iron rivet
entries.historical_notes: Rivets are the little tyrants holding armor civilization together.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate dome cap plus short cylinder stem; array along seams and plates.

entries.name: brass rivet
entries.historical_notes: Brass/copper alloy rivets make brigandine and leatherwork visually readable.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use warm metal shader; place on grid patterns for brigandine faces.

entries.name: leather thong
entries.historical_notes: Lacing systems are critical for lamellar and scale assemblies.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use bevelled curves threaded through holes; alternate over-under path.

entries.name: linen thread
entries.historical_notes: Thread/stitching defines construction and is a major close-up detail layer.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use stitch curves, dashed seam arrays, and bump maps for dense stitch zones.

entries.name: blackened finish
entries.used_for: plate armor finish, anti-glare, corrosion control aesthetic
entries.historical_notes: Blackened, browned, and blued finishes vary by period and process; model as finish families.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use metal shader with dark oxide mask and polished worn edges.

entries.name: tin/silvered surface
entries.historical_notes: Bright plating or surface treatment communicates rank and display armor.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use pale reflective metal material with worn-through edges.

entries.name: painted leather
entries.used_for: heraldic panels, fantasy armor, shield/brigandine facing
entries.historical_notes: Painted finishes make rank, faction, or ritual identity readable.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Add color mask layer, scratches, chipped edges, and dirt accumulation.

entries.name: measuring tape
entries.used_for: body measurements, garment and armor fit
entries.historical_notes: Use historically generalized measure cords/rules for older eras; modern tape for studio reconstruction.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curve strip with markings; useful as scene prop and measurement overlay.

entries.name: straightedge/ruler
entries.used_for: layout lines, scale drawings, plate templates
entries.historical_notes: Simple straight rules are universal shop logic. Boring, therefore immortal.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Thin rectangular bar with tick marks and worn edge.

entries.name: dividers/calipers
entries.used_for: transferring measurements, marking arcs, checking symmetry
entries.historical_notes: Dividers are central to pre-digital layout and repeat measurements.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Two tapered metal arms connected by hinge rivet; optional engraved scale.

entries.name: chalk/soapstone marker
entries.used_for: marking fabric, leather, and metal layout lines
entries.historical_notes: Any removable marker family works for patterning in the generator.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Small chalk stick plus faint white layout curves on material.

entries.name: paper/card template
entries.used_for: plate and garment pattern tests before material cutting
entries.historical_notes: Templates prevent expensive metal/leather mistakes, otherwise known as historical pain invoices.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Flat thin mesh with dashed fold/edge lines and labels.

entries.name: shears
entries.used_for: cutting cloth, light leather, pattern paper
entries.historical_notes: Large shears are workhorse tools for textile armor layers.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Two curved blade meshes, loop handles, central pivot rivet.

entries.name: leather knife
entries.historical_notes: Use broad generic category for skiving/cutting knives.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curved blade, cylinder handle, bevelled cutting edge.

entries.name: cold chisel
entries.historical_notes: A basic cutting/marking tool in metalwork; use with hammer.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Tapered cylinder with wedge tip and mushroomed striking end.

entries.name: snips
entries.historical_notes: Modern reconstruction analog for trimming sheet; older equivalent can be shears/chisels.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Compact hinged blade tool; add sheet offcuts nearby.

entries.name: forge hearth
entries.used_for: heating metal for forming and heat treatment
entries.historical_notes: Hearth style varies wildly by place and period; model as modular heat station.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Brick/stone box, coal bed, glow emission, soot gradients.

entries.name: bellows
entries.historical_notes: Bellows or forced air keeps forge temperature high enough for hot work.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Wooden wedge body, leather folds, nozzle cylinder, handle lever.

entries.name: tongs
entries.historical_notes: Different jaw shapes suit plates, bars, wire, and small fittings.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Two long tapered bars, hinge rivet, shaped jaws.

entries.name: quench tank
entries.used_for: cooling hot metal during heat treatment
entries.historical_notes: Liquid and process differ; for generator, represent as workshop station not recipe manual.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Vat mesh with dark liquid plane and steam/fog option.

entries.name: tempering oven/heat box
entries.historical_notes: Use as historical-to-modern abstraction for controlled heat stages.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Box/chamber prop with warm glow and thermometer/gauge optional.

entries.name: anvil
entries.historical_notes: Anvil forms vary; include block, horn, hardy hole as proxy features.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Block body, horn cone, beveled edges, hammered surface normal.

entries.name: stake anvil
entries.historical_notes: Stakes let the armor plate take controlled curves without becoming expensive scrap confetti.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Vertical cylinder post with mushroom, beak, or dome head variants.

entries.name: dishing stump
entries.historical_notes: Wood stumps absorb blows while helping create helmets, knees, elbows, and breastplates.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Cylinder stump, concave socket, strike marks, wood grain.

entries.name: sandbag
entries.historical_notes: Modern/proxy workshop support for controlled plate forming.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Squashed cloth sack with seam, filled deformation, dust marks.

entries.name: swage block
entries.historical_notes: A shape library in heavy metal form. Basically Blender modifiers but angry.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Rectangular block with repeated holes, grooves, hemispherical cavities.

entries.name: ball stake
entries.historical_notes: A ball stake is ideal for spherical curvature and helmet forms.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Metal sphere on cylinder post, optionally mounted to bench.

entries.name: cross-peen hammer
entries.historical_notes: Peen orientation helps move metal in specific directions.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Hammer head block, wedge peen, wood handle cylinder.

entries.name: raising hammer
entries.historical_notes: Used to compress and move metal into deeper forms.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Rounded head ends, slender handle, polished impact faces.

entries.name: planishing hammer
entries.historical_notes: Planishing refines the ugly goblin stage into respectable armor shape.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Smooth convex faces; pair with shiny planished plate sample.

entries.name: rawhide/wood mallet
entries.historical_notes: Softer hammers reduce surface damage while still moving material.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Large cylinder head with handle; worn edges and darker strike zones.

entries.name: punch
entries.used_for: rivet holes, lacing holes, decorative perforation
entries.historical_notes: Punch holes are central to riveted/laced armor construction.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Tapered metal cylinder; generate matching holes on plates.

entries.name: drift
entries.historical_notes: Drifts clean and size holes after punching.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Conical/oval tool, placed near punched plate sample.

entries.name: file
entries.used_for: edge cleanup, slot shaping, burr removal
entries.historical_notes: Files make fitted edges and hardware survivable to hands and cloth.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Thin rectangular bar with ridged normal texture and handle.

entries.name: reamer/awl
entries.used_for: leather holes, textile holes, small adjustments
entries.historical_notes: Awls are fundamental for leather and textile armor assembly.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Pointed cone shaft, bulb or cylinder handle.

entries.name: rivet set
entries.historical_notes: Sets preserve rivet shape and keep hardware visually consistent.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Short punch-like tool with concave end; pair with rivet dome sample.

entries.name: buckling bar/backing iron
entries.historical_notes: Backing support matters for strong clean rivets.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Small block or stake behind plates; add contact scuffs.

entries.name: clamps
entries.used_for: holding layers while drilling, riveting, stitching
entries.historical_notes: Use clamps as generic assembly helpers across workshop eras.
entries.blender_generator_notes: C-shaped frame with screw cylinder and contact pad.

entries.name: stitching needle
entries.historical_notes: Needles convert soft layers from floppy sadness into structure.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Fine cylinder with pointed end and eye hole proxy.

entries.name: thimble
entries.historical_notes: Tiny tool, huge reduction in thumb suffering.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Cup mesh with dimple normal texture.

entries.name: stitching pony/clamp
entries.historical_notes: A modern/reconstruction leatherwork helper; use as workshop fixture.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Two wooden jaws, hinge/bolt, base clamp.

entries.name: edge beveler
entries.historical_notes: Edge finishing keeps straps and panels from looking like cardboard cosplay tax fraud.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Small handled tool; add beveled leather strip output sample.

entries.name: wire drawplate
entries.historical_notes: Wire preparation is a core upstream process for mail production.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Rectangular metal plate with graduated holes; wire curves passing through.

entries.name: mandrel rod
entries.historical_notes: Ring size follows mandrel diameter; visual ring scale matters for mail realism.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Cylinder rod with spiral wire curve wrapped around it.

entries.name: ring cutters
entries.historical_notes: Represents the coil-to-ring production stage.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Tool plus scattered ring instances and cut coil segment.

entries.name: mail pliers
entries.historical_notes: Pliers allow ring manipulation at high repetition.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Two jaws, hinge rivet, textured handle grips.

entries.name: grindstone
entries.historical_notes: Grinding/polishing moves armor from forged object to finished surface.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Stone wheel cylinder, axle, water trough optional, dust/wear marks.

entries.name: polishing wheel
entries.historical_notes: More modern shop proxy; older equivalent can be abrasives and hand polishing.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Spinning disk object with radial blur option for render props.

entries.name: graver/burin
entries.historical_notes: Decorative linework separates plain combat kit from display armor.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Tiny chisel tool; generate incised curve grooves on plates.

entries.name: repousse punch
entries.historical_notes: Repoussé and chasing push metal into relief forms from front/back.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Set of rounded punches and relief plate sample normal/displacement.

entries.name: etching resist brush
entries.historical_notes: Represent etching as design process, not chemistry recipe.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Brush prop plus patterned dark resist curves on plate.

entries.name: body measurement mapping
entries.historical_notes: Armor must fit a moving body, not a heroic brick. Measure landmarks first.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate labeled points at neck, shoulder, chest, waist, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle.

entries.name: flat pattern drafting
entries.historical_notes: Flat templates become curved armor through forming, seams, or darts.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Store 2D pattern meshes that can be curved into 3D shells.

entries.name: allowance planning
entries.used_for: seam allowance, hems, rivet margins, overlap zones
entries.historical_notes: Margins prevent edge failure and give assembly room.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate highlighted border bands on pattern pieces.

entries.name: quilted padding
entries.used_for: gambeson, arming jacket, padded helmet liner
entries.historical_notes: Quilt channels hold stuffing in place and control compression.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Inflated panels separated by stitch grooves; add stitch curve arrays.

entries.name: layered textile lamination
entries.used_for: padded defense and structural cloth panels
entries.historical_notes: Multiple cloth layers can become surprisingly defensive when compressed and stitched.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Create nested cloth shells with exposed cross-section sample at edge.

entries.name: edge binding
entries.used_for: cloth, leather, mail borders, plate edges
entries.historical_notes: Binding prevents fray, protects edges, and gives a finished silhouette.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curve or strip mesh following garment perimeter with stitch holes.

entries.name: wet forming
entries.used_for: leather helmets, bracers, masks, fantasy armor
entries.historical_notes: Leather can be shaped around forms while damp, then dried into a stronger curve.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use deformed panel mesh around limb/helmet proxy; add shrink/warp effect.

entries.name: leather hardening proxy
entries.historical_notes: Historical hardening methods vary and are debated; model as a visual/structural category.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Increase panel stiffness, curled edges, darker surface finish.

entries.name: stamped leather decoration
entries.historical_notes: Stamped or tooled leather carries pattern identity without metalwork.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use normal/displacement patterns and repeated border motifs.

entries.name: wire drawing
entries.historical_notes: Wire production is the hidden bulk labor behind mail.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Represent with decreasing-diameter wire curves and drawplate prop.

entries.name: ring coiling
entries.historical_notes: Wire is wound around a mandrel to create consistent rings.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curve spiral around cylinder, then split into ring instances.

entries.name: 4-in-1 mail weave
entries.historical_notes: Classic mail visual pattern: each ring links through neighboring rings.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate instanced torus grid; LOD to normal map at distance.

entries.name: riveted ring closure
entries.historical_notes: Riveting ring overlaps improves durability compared with simple butted rings.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Flatten ring segment, overlap ends, add micro rivet dome.

entries.name: scale overlap
entries.historical_notes: Scales overlap like shingles to shed blows and movement friction.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Array small plates over cloth/leather backing with staggered rows.

entries.name: lamellar lacing
entries.historical_notes: Lamellar plates lace to each other instead of relying on a full backing sheet.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate rectangular lamella plates with hole pairs and cord curves.

entries.name: hidden plate riveting
entries.historical_notes: Plates hidden under textile/leather face show as rivet grids outside.
entries.blender_generator_notes: External cloth shell with repeated rivet domes; internal plate proxies optional.

entries.name: splint mounting
entries.historical_notes: Metal strips can reinforce soft backing while remaining flexible along one axis.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Array strips along forearm/shin; rivets along strap edges.

entries.name: dishing
entries.used_for: knees, elbows, helmet bowls, breastplate starts
entries.historical_notes: Plate is hammered into a hollow support to create concavity.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Start from flat circle/oval mesh, apply concave deformation and hammer normal map.

entries.name: raising
entries.historical_notes: Raising moves metal inward/upward with repeated controlled hammering.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate shell with compressed edge bands and radial hammer marks.

entries.name: sinking
entries.used_for: simple curves and shallow armor plates
entries.historical_notes: Sinking makes broad curves faster but can thin material.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use shallow deformation, smoother marks, broad panel curvature.

entries.name: planishing
entries.historical_notes: Planishing smooths and evens formed metal after rough shaping.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Reduce large dents, add small tight hammer-facet normal texture.

entries.name: rolling/hemming edge
entries.historical_notes: Rolled edges strengthen openings and reduce cutting hazards.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Add bevel/torus-like strip along plate perimeter.

entries.name: fluting
entries.historical_notes: Flutes strengthen plate and create a distinctive late medieval look.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Displace panel with repeated ridge grooves following limb/torso direction.

entries.name: articulated lames
entries.historical_notes: Overlapping plates let rigid armor bend without becoming a fancy coffin.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate stacked curved bands with sliding overlap and rivet pivots.

entries.name: strap and buckle suspension
entries.historical_notes: Suspension determines whether armor works on a body or just poses on a stand.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curved leather straps, rectangular buckle frames, prong, holes, wear marks.

entries.name: hinge construction
entries.historical_notes: Hinges manage openings where straps alone are clumsy.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Alternating cylinder sleeves around pin rod; animate rotation axis.

entries.name: hardening proxy
entries.historical_notes: Represent as material/state metadata, not a step-by-step thermal recipe.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Add metadata flag and subtle color/finish variation.

entries.name: tempering proxy
entries.historical_notes: Use as a generalized craft stage; exact temperatures are outside the generator's scope.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Optional amber/blue heat tint layer on test coupons or props.

entries.name: engraving
entries.historical_notes: Engraving cuts lines into the metal surface.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curve grooves or normal map linework on plates.

entries.name: etching pattern
entries.historical_notes: Model as patterned surface effect rather than workshop chemistry instructions.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use masks for dark incised patterns, borders, and heraldic motifs.

entries.name: repousse/chasing
entries.historical_notes: Metal is pushed into relief forms and refined from the front/back.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use displacement map or sculpted relief meshes on breastplate/helmet zones.

entries.name: gilding/silvering proxy
entries.historical_notes: Use as a finish family without chemical process details.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Material mask over ornaments, rivets, trim, and raised relief.

entries.name: polishing
entries.historical_notes: Degree of polish changes the whole armor mood: battlefield, parade, relic, nightmare dinnerware.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Increase roughness/metalness controls; add edge scratches and fingerprint haze.

entries.name: oil/wax coating
entries.historical_notes: Maintenance layer is part of armor life, not an afterthought.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Subtle sheen layer, dirt trapping, darker seam edges.

entries.name: gambeson/arming doublet
entries.historical_notes: A foundational padded garment for comfort, suspension, and protection.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate torso garment shell, quilt channel grid, sleeve seams, tie points.

entries.name: mail hauberk
entries.historical_notes: Flexible ring armor that drapes like metal fabric.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Use cloth-like garment mesh with mail texture/instanced rings at close range.

entries.name: scale cuirass
entries.historical_notes: Small plates attached to backing, overlapping downward/outward.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Array scales on front/back torso panels with row offset.

entries.name: lamellar harness
entries.historical_notes: Independent plates laced into a flexible shell.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate lamella rows with holes and cord curves crossing them.

entries.name: brigandine coat
entries.historical_notes: Outside often reads as textile/leather with rivet pattern; plates hidden inside.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Cloth shell, repeated rivets, optional internal plate debug layer.

entries.name: splinted vambrace
entries.historical_notes: Metal strips mounted over backing; useful for low-to-mid complexity armor.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Curved cuff mesh, strip arrays, strap buckles, rivets.

entries.name: plate breastplate
entries.historical_notes: Curved plate must fit breathing and arm movement, not just look shiny.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Generate mirrored torso shell, rolled edges, center ridge, strap anchors.

entries.name: helmet bowl
entries.historical_notes: Helmet families vary hugely; this is the core shell generator target.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Dome shell, brow band, cheek plates, nasal/visor variants.

entries.name: gauntlet
entries.historical_notes: Gauntlets are tiny articulated machines built to protect the most useful meat tools.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Palm leather base, finger lame chains, knuckle plates, wrist cuff.

entries.name: poleyn/knee armor
entries.historical_notes: Knee armor needs cup protection plus articulated bands for motion.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Cup shell, side wings, upper/lower lames, strap backside.

entries.name: pauldron/shoulder armor
entries.historical_notes: Shoulder armor must float with arm motion; rigid attachment looks broken fast.
entries.blender_generator_notes: Stacked curved lames over deltoid, strap/hinge to gorget or cuirass.

notes: Use stable lowercase identifiers in code.
Keep hazardous chemical or heat-treatment specifics out of generator docs.
Prioritize proxy geometry and LOD rules before realism.
